failure_summary.description: Calls used noncanonical values or incorrect parameter bindings, such as wrong field names, casing, or duplicated parameters.
A related but incorrect tool was selected for a requested outcome, and an unrelated tool was added.
Calls omitted or misapplied selectors implied by the requested entity type, or invented a restrictive value for an unspecified dimension.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers exact schema fields, canonical values, and parameter buckets, so those rules do not need repeating. These additions clarify two gaps visible in the batch: matching the requested entity rather than a related sub-entity, and applying documented search selectors implied by the wording without guessing values for unspecified dimensions.

edits.target: - Treat endpoint eligibility as a gate: confirm the endpoint's own operation and schema support the requested result kind and granularity, and can represent every compatible explicit qualifier. A topical neighbor or broader operation is not sufficient. A named provider or source is a hard constraint for that outcome; do not fulfill or supplement it with another provider when a fitting named-source endpoint exists.
edits.content: - Match the requested entity level and property as well as the topic: a result about a related component or sub-entity does not fulfill a request about the main entity, even when the search terms overlap.

edits.target: - Preserve requested search text, identifiers, and constraints; normalize only as the endpoint requires, without dropping meaningful words or substituting one value or geographic level for another. Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields, using accepted representations for enums and locales.
edits.content: - For optional search-mode or entity-type selectors, use the documented choice that matches an entity class or mode clearly identified in the request, even if the user did not phrase it as a filter. Do not choose an arbitrary restrictive value for another selector dimension the user left unspecified; omit it, or use a documented all/any value only when needed to express the requested scope.
